clue.text: Quit out-of-control press about one scandalous reporter

indicators.note: something out of control runs wild, so the letters of the following word are thrown into disorder
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap round the next piece

blocks.note: to quit a place is to go
taken as written, then jumbled
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A journalist walks out of a newspaper that has run amok over some scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' and 'reporter' make the clue look like a story about journalism; the press is only anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who spreads gossip passes on scandal about other people, a scandalmonger rather than a professional journalist.

clue.text: After one sees shape of egg, change egg supplier

blocks.note: the letter O is egg-shaped
to vary is to change

explanation.surface: Someone spots an oval outline and decides to switch to a different egg producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After one sees' just puts the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The ovary is the female organ that produces egg cells, so biologically it supplies eggs.

clue.text: Perhaps vampire slayer's assistant who has a real interest

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: someone who holds the wooden stake for the slayer
second meaning: a person with a share or concern in an enterprise

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: vampires are killed with a wooden stake through the heart, so a helper would hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: In business, a person with an investment or concern in an outcome is said to have a stake in it.

clue.text: Very inadequate way evidence is brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a path is a way
to cite is to bring forward as evidence

explanation.surface: A complaint that the route by which proof is produced in court is woefully poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic in its colloquial sense means feeble or miserably inadequate.

clue.text: Sought treasures for puzzling treatment in this?

indicators.note: puzzling suggests the words have been scrambled and must be worked out

blocks.note: every letter of both words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A treasure hunt that is itself the puzzling remedy being sought.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is fair warning: 'treatment' is looked up rather than given, since a thesaurus lists alternatives for a word like treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Roget's is the classic English reference book of synonyms, where any word, treatment included, has its alternatives listed.

clue.text: Mostly plain youth finds romance

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter of the next word is dropped

blocks.note: bald, meaning plain or unadorned, without its last letter
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A not-very-handsome young man nevertheless manages to find love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romance' looks like a love affair, but here it is a narrative poem; 'bald' as in a bald statement means plain.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance in the literary sense is a tale of adventure or love in verse, much like a narrative ballad.

clue.text: Ship I introduced to British military engineers

indicators.note: introduced to means put among, so this letter goes inside the following pair of pieces

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
taken as written
the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A naval vessel's commander meets a British army engineering unit.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers; the I slips in after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme is an ancient galley with two banks of oars, a type of warship.

clue.text: Unwilling to miss the last item in auction

indicators.note: missing the last means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: loth means reluctant or unwilling

explanation.surface: A reluctant bidder lets the final piece in the sale go by.
explanation.definitionFit: At an auction each numbered item or set of items offered for sale is called a lot.

clue.text: Close to hypotenuse, for example

blocks.note: first meaning: next to, beside
second meaning, split into three words: the hypotenuse is a long side of a right-angled triangle, in fact the longest

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning only works if the answer is broken into A LONG SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside is a preposition meaning beside or next to, which is what being close to something means.

clue.text: Empty tin into large tank

indicators.note: into means going inside, so this word is placed within the next

blocks.note: a vat is a large tank or tub
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An instruction to tip a can's contents into a big tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' reads as a verb, but the answer is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant is an adjective for something unoccupied or containing nothing, a synonym of the adjective empty.

clue.text: Going round allotment to east of Grindley Hollow

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its middle, so only the outside letters of the place name remain
in an across answer east is to the right, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the name
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Someone walks round an allotment east of a place called Grindley Hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grindley Hollow' looks like one place name; 'Hollow' is the instruction. An allotment is a rented garden plot in Britain, but here it means an allocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyration is the act of rotating or circling about a point, which is going round.

clue.text: Stamp fifty pence pieces?

blocks.note: first meaning: kind or character, as in a man of his stamp
second meaning, hedged by the question mark: one design or kind of coin, as collectors class coins

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is the shakier one: the fifty pence coin is taken as one sort among coins, the question mark admitting the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp and type both mean a kind or class, as in people of that stamp or that type.

clue.text: Unfortunately gloomy tone in which cricket may be studied

definitions.text: in which cricket may be studied

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters that follow come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: every letter of both words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy commentator's tone suits a dreary analysis of a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket wants to be the bat-and-ball game; here it is the chirping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Entomology is the scientific study of insects, and a cricket is an insect.

clue.text: Old streetwalker is comparatively weak, without promise

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the first piece goes around the second

blocks.note: lamer is the comparative of lame, meaning weak or feeble
to plight is to pledge or promise, as in plighting one's troth

explanation.surface: A former prostitute is described as rather feeble and lacking prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: Streetwalker usually means a prostitute; here it is someone who walked the streets at dusk lighting the gas lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamplighter was employed to go round the streets lighting and extinguishing street lamps, a job that has disappeared.

clue.text: Comic mouths off about religious subject

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
RI is religious instruction, the old school subject

explanation.surface: A comedian sounds off about religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouths off' reads as one phrasal verb, but it splits into fodder and anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorist is a writer or performer of humorous material, so a comic is one.

clue.text: Troubled, lacking guidance about where to find badger

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece encloses the second

blocks.note: unled means not led or guided
a sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious, having no directions to a place where badgers live.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsettled means disturbed or agitated in mind, a near synonym of troubled.

clue.text: A young girl, I'm bowled over by diamonds

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked down and scattered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
D is the card-playing abbreviation for diamonds; that the word's first four letters read backwards also spell the answer is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A young woman confesses she is dazzled by a gift of diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' belongs to the wordplay, so the definition is just 'young girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid is an old or literary word for a girl or young unmarried woman, as in maiden.

clue.text: Get drain adjusted for slope

indicators.note: adjusted means altered and set differently, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: every letter of both words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A builder's note to reset a drain so the water runs downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is the degree of incline of a surface, a synonym of slope.

clue.text: Exploited position of American media chief?

blocks.note: US is short for American
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a US media boss abused their position.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'media chief' is a loose description of an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To be used, in the sense of taken advantage of, is to be exploited.

clue.text: Sort of blind, almost, but finally recruited?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the blind loses its final letter
finally points to the last letter of the word that follows it

blocks.note: an en is a printer's measure, and in printing a sort is a single piece of type; this is the least certain piece of the parse
a roller blind winds up on a roller
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone who is more or less sightless nevertheless got signed up in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The roller blind, cut short, and the final D are clear; how 'Sort of' supplies the opening EN is uncertain, and the reading given is a best guess.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enrolled is to be signed up as a member, as a recruit is taken on.

clue.text: Sailor told to leave for showing a lack of attention

blocks.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
someone sent away has been told to go

explanation.surface: A sailor is ordered off the ship for being inattentive on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent describes a distracted, faraway look or manner, as in absent-minded, so it shows inattention.

clue.text: Visualised dramatic scenario where broody star runs out

indicators.note: something that runs out gets loose and scattered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: every letter of both words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A film plot where the moody leading actor storms off the set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs out' looks like the star walking off, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyboard is a sequence of drawings laying out the scenes of a film or play shot by shot before filming.

clue.text: Insult having English on the Rock

indicators.note: on in an across clue means attached after, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: Gibraltar, known as the Rock, is shortened to Gib
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone takes offence at English people living on Gibraltar.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibraltar is the British territory at the tip of Spain, nicknamed the Rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibe is a taunting or mocking remark, a synonym of an insult.

clue.text: Bishop leads over newspaper that's brought up big payment to banker?

indicators.note: leads means is at the front, so only the first letter of the next word is used
in a down answer, bringing something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the first letter of the word
the Sun, a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A churchman is outraged that a paper has raised the subject of bankers' huge payouts.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: bankers are famous for large bonuses.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an extra sum paid on top of salary, and banks are notorious for very large ones.

clue.text: Everyone helps tidy away — a sign of health and safety?

definitions.text: a sign of health and safety?

blocks.note: all means everyone
to clear things is to tidy them away

explanation.surface: Office staff clearing up together, ticking a box for workplace health and safety rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Health and safety' suggests workplace regulations, but the definition just means a signal that things are well and safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-clear is a signal that danger has passed, as after an air raid or a medical check.

clue.text: Vintage, as applied to wine, is a lot of nonsense

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: crud is slang for rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses wine talk about vintages as mostly rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cru, French for growth, names a vineyard or the wine graded from it, as in grand cru, a term like vintage.

clue.text: Area is ten by ten in feet, but half hidden

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side
in means placed inside, so the side-by-side pieces go within what remains
with half of it hidden, only part of the word shows, its outer pair kept

blocks.note: half of the word's letters taken away, leaving its outer two
X is the Roman numeral ten
taken as written

explanation.surface: A floor measurement: a room ten feet by ten feet, partly out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten by ten in feet' reads as a measurement; it is one ten as a Roman numeral and one written out, placed inside what is left of the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent is the size or scale of a space, and area is how much surface a region covers.

clue.text: Fit plug precisely

blocks.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an ad
just means exactly or precisely

explanation.surface: An instruction to insert an electrical plug exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests something electrical; it is a promotional mention.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something is to alter it so it fits or suits, the verb sense of fit.

clue.text: Burlesque artist posed in front of one topless joint

indicators.note: in front of means coming before, so these pieces lead the rest
topless means with the top removed, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so posed gives sat
one is the Roman numeral I
the wrist is a joint

explanation.surface: A burlesque dancer posing topless in front of a sleazy club.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlesque suggests strip shows, which 'posed' and 'topless' play on, but its older meaning is mocking parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A satirist mocks people or institutions through ridicule, and burlesque in its literary sense is mocking parody.
